newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reserves jump crowns golden week for S.Africa mkts.
newsitem.headline: Reserves jump crowns golden week for S.Africa mkts.

text.p: Far better than expected gold and foreign exchange reserves figures for January crowned the best week for South African financial markets on Friday since the rand meltdown started a year ago.

Gross reserves of 11.76 billion in January, up from 10.31 billion in December, beat even the most optimistic forecasts. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a range of 10.5 to 11.5 billion with the consensus at 11.2 billion.
The January reserves were the highest since March 1996, with a jump in foreign assets of 1.83 billion rand more than offseting a 369 million rand decline in gold holdings.

The sharp increase reflects the flood of portfolio funds which have flowed into the country so far this year. Foreigners were net buyers of more than 3.2 billion rand worth of South Africa bonds in the year up to Thursday, according to Bond Exchange figures.

Growing confidence in South African assets based on expectations of a sharply improving trade balance this year and a stabilising rand, were boosted on Friday by President Nelson Mandela's upbeat address at the opening of parliament.
That helped to lift the rand to its best levels in 6-1/2 months against the dollar while long bond yields fell to 5-1/2 month lows.

On the Johannesburg Stock Exchnage, renewed foreign interest lifted industrial shares sharply and the bourse recorded the highest weekly market turnover in its 109-year history. Trading value amounted to 4.3 billion rand, surpassing the previous record of 3.3 billion rand set for the week ended November 15, 1996.
